concept: Display is the one window of a dial unit that says what the device is doing now, recessed into the plastic body, drawn as LCD segments or OLED text, announced politely and never pressed.

default_to_avoid.pattern: dashboard display: a stat card or KPI tile with a big bold number and a coloured up/down delta
default_to_avoid.why_not: A KPI tile floats on the page and tells change by colour, while P2 asks for a window recessed into the body that says the state in numbers or words.

default_to_avoid.pattern: glowing neon LCD display with a blurred text-shadow on the digits
default_to_avoid.why_not: LCD segments do not emit light, so P6 allows no glow there and the reading must stay crisp at 4.5:1.

references.source: Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): a recessed grey-green LCD with dark segments, right-aligned digits
Braun AB 312 radio clock: one window for the time, unit and mode printed small beside it
apps/lab/anchor/anchor.js: the anchor card A's 7-segment SVG renderer segText (D-001)

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The root carries elevation.well, shade on the top-left inner edge and a lit edge bottom-right, never a cast shadow.

derivation.consequence: the window is a rounded rectangle whose radius nests in the body (inner = outer − inset)
derivation.form: border-radius is the container's outer radius minus its inset, read from --display-outer and --display-inset, defaulting to corner.inner.

derivation.consequence: two display families, LCD (dark grey segments on grey-green, ≥4.5:1) and OLED (white on near-black)
derivation.form: kind lcd paints display.lcd-bg with display.lcd-ink segments and display.lcd-ghost unlit ones; kind oled paints display.oled-bg with display.oled-ink.

derivation.consequence: tabular numerals, a 7-segment face for LCD values, the system grotesk for OLED text
derivation.form: LCD values are SVG segment cells on a fixed pitch with the unit in the grotesk beside them; OLED sets value and detail in the grotesk with tabular figures.

derivation.consequence: values change at once; only a segment's on/off fades, ≤80ms
derivation.form: Only the fill of each segment polygon transitions, over motion.segment, and nothing moves or counts up between readings.

derivation.consequence: the display is a live region (polite) and never a control
derivation.form: The root is role status with aria-live polite and a label, holds no focusable element and reads the full reading as text.

derivation.consequence: no gradients, no glow except P2's emitters
derivation.form: LCD segments carry no shadow, filter or blur; only flat ink on the flat grey-green window.

derivation.consequence: fixed positions, so a unit's layout does not reflow between states
derivation.form: The digits prop pads short readings with unlit cells so the window keeps one width while the value changes.

options.name: segment window, unit beside the value, detail inside
digits-only window, unit and detail printed on the body
text window, grotesk value line and detail line

variants.reason: A keeps the whole reading inside one recessed window with the LCD segment face P2 asks for and right-aligned tabular cells that never shift (P6); B splits the state across two surfaces so the window alone no longer tells it, and C's grotesk-only layout is kept as the oled kind, where P2 wants the system grotesk.

root.why: The window is a recess in the body with inverse light and a radius nested inside the unit's corner.

lcd.why: The LCD family puts dark grey segments on grey-green at more than 4.5:1 for every glyph.

oled.why: The OLED family puts white grotesk text on near-black, the one window allowed to emit light.

sm.why: Small windows draw 24px segment cells for secondary readings inside a dense unit or list row.

md.why: The default window draws 40px segment cells, the size of the anchor card's reading.

lg.why: Large windows draw 56px segment cells for the one reading a whole sheet is about.

reading.why: The full reading is kept as hidden text so assistive tech hears the value, unit and detail together.

face.why: The drawn face holds the detail and the value line on the window's inner inset, hidden from assistive tech.

detail.why: One short detail line in the grotesk at caption size says the mode or the target next to the value.

line.why: The value line keeps tabular numerals with the unit beside the value, right-aligned on LCD and start-aligned on OLED.

seg.why: The LCD value is drawn as 7-segment SVG cells on a fixed pitch because no segment font ships with dial.

on.why: A lit segment is LCD ink at more than 4.5:1 on the grey-green, flat with no glow.

off.why: An unlit segment stays as a faint ghost so the cell grid reads as a real LCD and widths stay fixed.

unit.why: The unit is printed in the system grotesk at label size beside the value, never as a segment.

data-glow.why: The OLED window is one of the emitters P2 allows, so in the dark edition it gives off a little of its own light, gone within 32px; in light it gives off none, and LCD windows never do.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion segments switch on and off at once, with no fade between readings at all.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the window keeps a real border and lit segments take the system text colour so the reading survives.

fill.why: Only a segment's on and off state fades, within 80ms, so the new value is there at once.
